agreements: All three identify the exact developer content as You are a model that can do function calling with the following functions, with developer as the API role and no trailing punctuation or whitespace.

All three agree that the function declaration begins with declaration: followed by the bare function name and that all string values, including type names, enum values, and required entries, are enclosed by escape tokens.
All three identify STRING and OBJECT as the escaped, uppercased serialized forms of the JSON type names.
All three recognize that the documentation examples disagree about declaration whitespace and that the installed processor or chat template is the authoritative source.
All three describe the six function-control tokens as three start/end pairs and treat escape as a separate delimiter.
All three describe the turn framing as start-of-turn plus role and newline, followed by content and end-of-turn, with a model generation-prompt suffix.
All three agree that max_new_tokens=128 is documented and that temperature, top_p, top_k, and do_sample are not explicitly specified in the declared pages.

All three agree that Hugging Face's shown call omits sampling arguments and therefore uses its non-sampling greedy default, while distinguishing that conclusion from an explicitly documented temperature value.
All three agree that google/functiongemma-270m-it works zero-shot for the documented basic single-turn cases and that fine-tuning is not a prerequisite for those cases.
All three note the checkpoint's stated lack of explicit multi-turn and multi-step training and the role of better descriptions or fine-tuning for difficult semantic cases.
All three flag the repository's missing mappings for the function-call and function-response control tokens.
All three recommend processor-derived serialization and engine-side comparisons rather than continued speculation about the developer wording.

limitations: It calls declaration whitespace the most likely mismatch even though the supplied context says the 98-token prefill is already bit-exact, which underweights the stronger engine-side diagnosis.
The section labeled as a complete verbatim prompt abbreviates the declaration with an ellipsis, so it is not by itself a fully copyable literal prompt.
Some repository findings, detokenizer properties, and stop-token details are presented beside official statements even though they are not all established by the three declared documents.
The source mapping is generally clear but less systematic than candidate B's page-by-page labeling.
risks: A user might unnecessarily rewrite an already token-exact prompt to chase the whitespace discrepancy instead of first comparing forward-pass logits and cache boundaries.
Treating every inferred detokenizer or stop detail as an official serialization rule could cause an implementation to diverge from the shipped processor template.
strengths: States the exact developer content with the required absence of trailing punctuation or whitespace and places it immediately before the declaration token.
Provides a concrete serialized weather declaration and correctly distinguishes bare structural keys from escaped string values, including uppercased STRING and OBJECT type names.
Documents the role and turn framing, BOS placement, generation-prompt suffix, function-call grammar, response grammar, and the observed post-tool continuation.
Correctly explains that the examples use the unmodified checkpoint zero-shot and that fine-tuning is a mitigation for semantic or multi-turn limitations rather than a prerequisite for basic calling.
Identifies that only max_new_tokens=128 and the EOS pad token are documented generation settings, while labeling greedy decoding as an inference from Hugging Face defaults.
Flags the four function-call/response control tokens missing from the repository's exact-match token table.
candidate_assessments.summary: A detailed and implementable specification covering the exact developer trigger, declaration grammar, control tokens, turn layout, generation settings, zero-shot behavior, and tool-response continuation. It is especially useful for explaining serialization details and connecting the documentation to the repository's token-table gap.
useful_contributions: Supplies the most complete exact weather declaration, including the unusual spaces before selected closing braces.
Explains why declaration values, enum members, required entries, and uppercase type names must all use escape delimiters.
Provides a concrete model continuation showing the call, response, and final answer within one rendered model turn.
Provides actionable checks for BOS ownership, greedy decoding, missing control-token mappings, and post-call stopping.

Its full London prompt is reconstructed rather than printed verbatim by the declared documentation, as the response itself acknowledges.
The proposed alphabetical ordering is inferred from examples rather than stated as a general template contract.
The statement that BOS is emitted by the template but not by the raw-prefill path could be read ambiguously; the raw file prompt must still match the processor output containing BOS.
risks: If followed literally, whitespace normalization could alter a prompt that is already processor-correct.
The reconstructed prompt or observed role ownership could be mistaken for a stable template guarantee instead of something that must be verified against the installed tokenizer and chat template.
strengths: Uses explicit source labels for the formatting, Hugging Face, and full-sequence pages, making individual claims relatively easy to audit.
States the exact developer message, serialized declaration grammar, escaped type names, array-item escaping, literal quote handling, and bare numeric values.
Provides a reconstructed literal London prompt while clearly warning that its exact bytes still need to come from the shipped chat template.
Explains the distinction between rendered role names such as model and message-API roles such as assistant and tool.
Correctly concludes that the documented basic examples are zero-shot and that multi-turn, multi-step, and indirect-language cases may require fine-tuning or better tool descriptions.
Provides a focused debugging sequence: compare against Hugging Face off-Pi, inspect the first generated position, verify numerics, complete the token table, and diff any independently written card.
Explicitly records documentation ambiguities instead of presenting them as settled facts.
candidate_assessments.summary: A carefully source-labeled response that separates documented facts, observed examples, template-dependent behavior, and repository diagnostics. It addresses all five requested areas and gives a strong engine-side debugging path conditioned on the already bit-exact prefill.
useful_contributions: Best organizes claims by declared source and clearly identifies which formatting details are direct rules versus observations.
Connects the exact prefill match to the conclusion that prompt wording and escaping no longer explain the observed failure.
Provides concrete repository checks for first-position handling, KV-cache alignment, BF16 behavior, control-token coverage, and byte-level template comparison.
Captures the documented mitigation hierarchy for weak tool descriptions and the checkpoint's stated training scope.

limitations: It overstates the documentation by describing prose rambling as a documented consequence of omitting the developer message and by calling a 0.81 prose probability the documented limited-description symptom.
The limited-description example concerns an indirect hot-or-cold query, so it does not establish why an explicit London query with a processor-identical prompt fails.

It suggests that the full-sequence declaration contains comma-space separators, which is stronger than the concrete rendered examples support; the clearly demonstrated discrepancy concerns spaces before selected closing braces.
Its London prompt is explicitly reconstructed, so it should not be presented as an exact official byte string without processor verification.
Adding end_function_call as an optional stop is not supported by the declared documentation's specific additional-stop statement.
risks: The unsupported 0.81-to-limited-description diagnosis could send the debugging effort toward schema-description tuning even though the failing query is explicit and its token IDs match.
Stopping on end_function_call without defining how the expected response prefix is re-fed could truncate or alter the documented continuation protocol.
strengths: Correctly gives the developer trigger and explains that the schema is supplied separately through the tools argument rather than appended to the developer text.
Covers escaped strings, uppercased types, escaped enum and required values, literal quotes, bare numeric values, and the need to preserve processor-generated whitespace.
Describes BOS, role framing, turn delimiters, the three pairs of function-control tokens, the separate escape delimiter, and the post-tool rendering.
Correctly identifies max_new_tokens=128 as the only documented generation budget and greedy decoding as the Hugging Face default rather than a separately documented sampling recommendation.
States the zero-shot and fine-tuning caveats clearly, including the trained single-turn and parallel scope and the lack of explicit multi-turn training.

Finds repository-specific weaknesses that are directly relevant to implementation: an incomplete control-token table, a decode loop lacking the documented response stop, and the need to compare engine numerics and logits.

useful_contributions: Makes the template-derived whitespace rule operational by directing the implementer to generate and compare the actual repr output.
Provides concrete instructions for obtaining the four missing token IDs from tokenizer metadata rather than guessing them.
Identifies a concrete repository stop-loop defect that could append junk after a valid function call.
Adds useful residual checks involving attention configuration, RoPE, normalization, softcapping, masks, and first-token logit comparison.

positions.position: Treats the full-sequence decoded processor output, including spaces before two closing braces, as the authoritative byte rendering and calls that difference the most likely mismatch.
Acknowledges that the examples conflict and says to use apply_chat_template as ground truth, but also advises emitting no stray spaces.
Treats both snippets as illustrative and says the actual processor output, including whatever spacing it emits, must be copied verbatim.

conflicts.resolution: Use processor.apply_chat_template with the installed model snapshot as the sole byte-level authority. Preserve unusual spaces exactly and assert equality against the resulting token IDs. Do not normalize either documentation example. Given the reported 98-of-98 prefill match, this discrepancy is not the cause of the current failing run unless the independently supplied raw card differs elsewhere.

conflicts.resolution: Do not diagnose either whitespace or tool-description weakness from the supplied evidence. must_avoid: Do not hand-copy either declaration example or normalize processor-produced spaces.
Do not claim that the documentation specifies temperature=0, top_p, top_k, or any other numeric sampling values.
Do not claim that fine-tuning is required for the documented single-turn or parallel function-calling examples.
Do not treat the reconstructed London prompt as byte-exact without a processor-level assertion.
Do not infer or invent the four missing control-token IDs.
Do not treat omission of the developer message, declaration whitespace, or an indirect-description failure as a proven cause of the current bit-exact failing run.
Do not present end_function_call as a documented stop without defining the corresponding continuation protocol.

must_include.contribution: Include its complete escaped weather declaration, concrete post-tool continuation, and explanation of escaped arrays, uppercased types, and bare numeric response values.
Use its page-by-page citation mapping, explicit documentation-versus-inference distinctions, reconstructed London prompt, and prioritized engine-side debugging checks.
Include its repository-specific stop-loop finding, tokenizer-derived control-token ID procedure, and residual attention, RoPE, normalization, and numeric checks.

must_resolve: Make the installed processor and chat template authoritative for every byte and token ID, including unusual whitespace that differs from prose examples.
State explicitly that the given 98-of- token prefill match rules out developer wording, declaration escaping, and whitespace as explanations for the current output failure.

Separate documented facts from inferences: max_new_tokens=128 is documented; greedy behavior follows from omitted sampling arguments and Hugging Face defaults; temperature, top_p, and top_k have no documented recommended numeric values.
Keep start_function_response as the documented additional stop while treating other stop choices as implementation-specific and requiring consistent history reconstruction.
Require all four missing function-control token IDs to be read from the installed tokenizer or token JSON, never inferred.
Use the explicit London query and processor-identical token IDs when comparing first-token logits; do not infer a limited-description failure from the 0.81 value alone.
